requirements.verbatim_text: Questions or Clarifications Submission Deadline 7/15/2026, 10:30 AM
Courtesy Review of HUB Subcontracting Plan (HSP) Submission Deadline 07/21/2026, 10:30 AM
Response Deadline: Responses to this IFB must be received 7/31/2026, 10:30 AM
Anticipated Contract Start Date 9/01/2026

To be considered for award, Bidders must submit a comprehensive Response which includes all required information and documentation as outlined in this IFB to ensure the Bidder meets all requirements, possesses the required experience and qualifications, and has the capacity to provide the services described in this IFB. See Appendix A, Submission Instructions and Response Checklist.
Bidders should NOT submit exceptions to this IFB which could result in disqualification of a Response. No changes to a Response can be made after the submission deadline.

No assumptions should be included in a Response. The inclusion of assumptions could result in disqualification of a Response. Instead, a Bidder should advance assumptions and seek clarification of a section of this IFB, any Exhibits or attachments, in the form and manner required in Section 6.7 IFB Questions or Clarifications.

Responses must be received by HHSC prior to the Response Deadline as indicated in the Procurement Schedule. Every Bidder is solely responsible for ensuring its Response is received by HHSC before the Response Deadline in accordance with all requirements regarding submission.

By submitting a Response, the Bidder represents and warrants that the individual submitting the Response, inclusive of the documents made part of the Response, is authorized to sign on behalf of the Bidder, and to bind the Bidder under any Contract that may result from this IFB.
Bidders may withdraw or amend their Responses at any time prior to the Response Deadline by e-mailing the point of contact listed in Section 6.1 (Sole Point of Contact and Communications).
The e-mail subject line for withdrawal or response amendment should contain the IFB number as indicated on the cover page of this IFB.
Bidders shall NOT use the e-mail address above for submission of a Response to this IFB. See Appendix A for submission requirements.

Bidders shall direct all communications, including questions or clarifications relating to this IFB, by e-mail to the HHSC PCS Sole Point of Contact named in Section 6.1 (Sole Point of Contact and Communications); communications by phone will not be accepted except for purposes such as instructing a potential Respondent through an IT system or website referenced in this Solicitation.

All other communications between a Bidder and HHSC agency staff concerning this IFB are prohibited. In no instance is a Bidder to discuss cost information regarding this IFB with the HHSC PCS Sole Point of Contact or any other HHSC staff. Failure to comply with these requirements may result in disqualification of the Response.

Should Bidders have questions regarding proper completion of the HUB Subcontracting Plan, the HUB Coordinator may be contacted at HHSCHUB@hhs.texas.gov. The Sole Point of Contact, Section 6.1, must be copied on the e-mail.
By submitting a Response to this IFB, Bidder agrees that its Response will remain a firm and binding offer for 240 days, as stated in the HHS Solicitation Affirmations (Exhibit A).

Bidders must notify the Sole Point of Contact, Section 6.1, of any ambiguity, conflict, discrepancy, exclusionary specification, omission, or other error in the IFB in the manner and by the deadline for submitting questions.

HHSC will allow questions and requests for clarification regarding this IFB if submitted by e-mail to the Sole Point of Contact, Section 6.1, by the deadline established in the Procurement Schedule (cover page of this IFB) or deadlines established in subsequent Addenda.

All questions and requests for clarification must be submitted by e-mail and include the following information: a) IFB Number and Title of IFB (cover page of this IFB) must be included in the e-mail subject line and in the e-mail body; b) Section or Paragraph number from this IFB; c) Page Number of this IFB; d) Exhibit name, Section or Paragraph, page number from the Exhibit; e) Language, Topic, Section Heading being questioned or requested for clarification; f) Requestor Contact Information must be included in the body of the e-mail.

Bidder must acknowledge receipt of any addenda by signing and returning SOLICITATION ADDENDUM ACKNOWLEDGEMENT FORM posted to the ESBD with your solicitation response in accordance with the submission options outlined in the Solicitation.
Note: ONLY Commissioned Texas Peace Officers shall provide security services.
Recruit and maintain a pool of Commissioned Peace Officers to deliver armed security services at all HHSC service locations located in Region 6.

Schedule and notify Commissioned Peace Officers of duty assignments. Assignments shall be scheduled in a matter that ensures a Commissioned Peace Officer is on duty continuously during standard office hours of the assigned service location.

Conduct weekly on-site supervisor or upper management visits to monitor Commissioned Peace Officer's performance. Performance is measured against SOW that is listed in section 7 and the site-specific Post Orders assignment given service manager or point of contact.

Address performance issues and all other activities related to the effective and efficient management and administration of the Region 6 security SOW. The contractor will use the SOW and the post orders to address performance issues and all other activities related to effective and efficient management.

Provide updates and/or other security related information with the HHSC Contract Manager and/or designee, as deemed necessary. Reports should be provided monthly to capture routine day-to-day activities. However, non-routine/emergency incidents should be reported verbally within 2 -hours of the incident. The contractor must provide a written statement/report of said incident within 24 hours.
Manage all Commissioned Peace Officers at all services locations, at all times, including, but not limited to, ensuring Commissioned Peace Officers report for duty at assigned times and locations.
In the event a Commissioned Peace Officer is unable to report for duty, ensure a qualified replacement Peace Office is provisioned to avoid an interruption in service.

Provide a replacement Commissioned Peace Officer within two (2) hours after notification when an assigned Commissioned Peace Officer departs a service location due to an emergency. The notification shall be to the Contract Manager from the contractor/and or HHSC onsite staff.
Coordinate with HHSC for provision of services outside of standard office hours, weekends, and/or official State Holidays.
Always be in full Commissioned Peace Officer uniform, neat in appearance, and have no visible impairment when present at an assigned service location.

Remain at the designated security station located in the service location lobby area and notify the local HHSC Office Coordinator and/or designee prior to leaving the post for any reason other than to respond to a security emergency or incident.

Request any person who is continuously loud or boisterous at a service location to lower their volume or leave the premises. In the event of a conflict or disturbance, the Peace Office shall make his/her presence known and render assistance, as needed.
Inform the service location management or HHSC Office Coordinator when there is cause to expel an individual from state property and cite the reason(s) for the action prior to its execution.

Not occupy a private office at a service location or engage in lengthy personal conversations or other activities other than conducting continuous security services as specified herein. Interactions with state employees and clients shall remain professional, brief, and necessary for performance of the security services.
Not perform clerical, administrative, or non-security-related work such as setting up a conference room, moving boxes, or other logistical functions other than security services.
Become familiar with emergency phone numbers and service location evacuation plans.

In the event of a security incident, complete a Security Incident Report provided by the Contractor and forward a copy to the HHSC Contract Manager within twenty-four (24) hours of the incident. The report shall be a comprehensive and accurate account of the details related to the incident.

Utilize Time Sheet Management System (TSMS) to submit hours worked at a service location. HHSC will assign each Commissioned Peace Officer a unique ID that allows them to log in to TSMS. Commissioned Peace Officers shall phone in from the service location to gain access to TSMS. Commissioned Peace Officers shall not access TSMS on behalf of any other Commissioned Peace Officer.
Refrain from the use of personal cell phone devices while on duty at service location.

Contractor shall perform the contracted services, including any minor adjustment call-back services, Monday through Friday between the hours 7 a.m. to 7 p.m (Central Time). Contractor shall not interfere with normal flow of HHSC business at any service location.
Contractor shall respond to all service calls within four (4) hours of HHSC request, unless the Response Deadline is extended by the HHSC Contract Manager.

Any services performed outside of standard office hours 7 a.m. to 7 p.m Central Time) must be requested and approved in writing by the HHSC Contract Manager and will be paid at the rate stated in Exhibit C – Pricing Sheet.

Contractor shall respond to requests for emergency deployment of Commissioned Peace Officers to specific locations within one (1) hour of notification from HHSC and continue work until the services requested are complete to the satisfaction of HHSC.
Bidder shall submit documentation of experience and qualifications with Response, if requested in Exhibit C– Pricing Sheet.

Bidder shall have relevant experience required for the performance of the services outlined in this IFB. The minimum experience required for the vendor and Commissioned Peace Officers is three (3) years.
Bidder's personnel to be assigned to perform the services must be fully trained and, at minimum, have three (3) years' relevant experience as Commissioned Peace Officer.
Required Licensure. The bidder shall ensure their personnel have all required licenses through TCOLE to be a Commissioned Peace Officer
All Contractor or Subcontractor personnel assigned to perform the services must be at least 18 years of age.

Bidder must provide a minimum of three (3) verifiable references for current or previous contracts of the same size and for similar or same services within the last five (5) years in Exhibit D – Bidder Reference Form and return with Response.

In no case shall Contractor or Subcontractors make duplicates of any issued keys or access cards. Contractor may be required to reimburse HHSC for replacement costs for any lost keys or access cards or for those not returned at the expiration of the Contract.
Contractor shall furnish all labor, tools, transportation, equipment, materials, and supplies, as necessary, to perform the services and/or provide the goods, as required.
Contractor shall be responsible for supervision of its employees and Subcontractor employees, together with clean up and proper disposal of any site work waste.
Contractor shall complete an Incident Report and submit to HHSC, upon completion.

Contractors' Commissioned Peace Officers must maintain the required Commissioned Peace Officer licensure issued by TCOLE and Contractor shall ensure such licensure remains in good standing throughout the term of the Contract.

Contractor shall comply with all federal, state and local laws, statutes, ordinances, rules and regulations, and the orders and decrees of any court or administrative bodies or tribunals in any matter affecting the performance of the Contract including, if applicable, workers' compensation laws, minimum and maximum salary and wage statutes and regulations, and licensing laws and regulations.

All Contractor employees, and Subcontractor's employees, if applicable, assigned to perform services under the Contract, must be trained and experienced in the type of work to be performed. Contractor shall provide adequate training, including the roles, responsibilities and technical aspects of the work, to all personnel assigned to perform services under the Contract.
Contractor shall provide and allow only trained and qualified personnel to perform the required services under the Contract.

Contractor shall provide current copies of the completed training(s) and the license or accreditation certificate related to the training upon request by the HHSC Contract Manager. This requirement also applies to Subcontractor(s) and Subcontractor's personnel who may be used in the performance of services under the Contract.

Contractor shall not allow any visitors, spouses, children or other relatives of the Contractor's or Subcontractor's employees to be on HHSC property in connection with the Contract during working hours.
Contractor shall be responsible for all employment taxes and other payroll withholding for its employees.
Contractor shall be responsible and liable for the safety and health of its personnel while they are performing services for HHSC and while on HHSC premises.

Contractor shall be responsible for verifying that all of its employees assigned to perform services under the Contract are in compliance with all requirements of the Immigration Reform and Control Act of 1986, Public Law 99-603, which became effective November 6, 1986, and any subsequent amendments.

Contractor shall utilize the U.S. Department of Homeland Security's E-Verify system throughout the term of the contract to determine eligibility of (A) all persons employed by Contractor to perform services in Texas; and (B) all persons, including subcontractors, assigned by Contractor to perform services under the contract within the United States of America.
Contractor and its assigned employees or Subcontractor and Subcontractor employees assigned to perform services must have all applicable permits, licenses, accreditations, and insurance coverage.
Contractor shall be responsible for the security, maintenance, loss, or damage to its equipment or its Subcontractor's equipment while on HHSC premises.

Contractor or an independent third party will need to conduct comprehensive, statewide Texas Department of Public Safety (DPS) criminal and sex offender background checks on all Contractor personnel (e.g., permanent and temporary personnel and/or Subcontractor and Subcontractor personnel) who will be assigned to perform services under the Contract.
The Contractor shall be responsible for all expenses associated with background checks
Background checks must be conducted prior to any Contractor or Subcontractor personnel arriving on state property and commencing the provision of services under the contract.

Background checks shall include, but not be limited to, Social Security Number verification. Statewide criminal and sex offender background checks shall include, but is not limited to, records of Texas counties and out-of-state jurisdictions based on current and previous addresses of key personnel for the last seven (7) years.

Personnel with sex offender, child or adult abuse, or fraud convictions may not provide services under the contract or provided access to HHSC property, facilities, or documents in connection with the Contract.
Personnel with misdemeanor convictions are subject to prior review and approval by HHSC before being assigned to conduct services under this Contract.
Contractor shall comply with the Department of Public Safety (DPS) guidelines for Background Checks, included as Exhibit G– DFPS Custodial and Security Guard Background Check Information.

Contractor shall provide qualified replacements for any employees or Subcontractor employee providing services for HHSC who may be absent at an assigned service location for any reason. Contractor shall provide relief personnel as necessary and/or work overtime at no cost to HHSC, to ensure that the requirements of this Contract are performed and accomplished as required.
Contractor shall have an active telephone service answered during normal business hours. Normal business hours are between 8 a.m. and 5 p.m. Monday through Friday, unless otherwise stated in the IFB.
Contractor shall maintain two (2) points of contract and a phone number that is available 24 hours a day, seven (7) days a week.

Contractor and Subcontractor's performance of the services required under the Contract shall comply with all applicable state laws, statutes, rules, regulations, and HHSC and service location requests, regarding personal and professional conduct. All Contractor personnel must always conduct themselves in a businesslike and professional manner.

Contractor shall provide a competent supervisor(s) if the service location is at an HHSC facility. A Supervisor may be considered a roving Supervisor that monitors more than one (1) location subject to prior review and approval by the HHSC Contract Manager.
All supervisors must be able to communicate in English verbally and in writing. Supervisor(s) shall be knowledgeable of the requirements set forth in this the Statement of Work and the Contract.
Contractor and supervisor(s) shall continuously monitor and maintain awareness, by personal inspection, of the quality and completeness of the services being performed.

At the request of HHSC, Contractor must replace any Contractor or Subcontractor personnel who are not adequately performing the required services or who are unable to work effectively with the HHSC Contract Manager or other HHSC staff. Contractor shall provide qualified replacement personnel who have completed the required training as required by the Contract.

The use or possession of any kind of intoxicants or illegal drugs by Contractor (or any of its Subcontractors) employees while on duty at HHSC service locations, including the building and grounds, is prohibited.
All HHSC facilities are non-smoking buildings. Contractor's and Subcontractor's employees are prohibited from smoking in all non-designated areas.
All Contractor and Subcontractor employees are required to wear company uniforms and identifying badges while providing services in or on HHSC service locations.
Contractor and Subcontractor's uniform apparel must be of one standard color or design.

All Contractor and Subcontractor personnel must prominently display their company identification badges or the company name and employee's name (first and/or last) must be on their shirt, T-shirt, or smock.

The final HSP must be submitted by the Response Deadline identified in the Procurement Schedule (cover page of this IFB) or deadlines established in subsequent Addenda. Responses received without a properly completed HSP will be disqualified.

To request a courtesy review, submit the completed HSP including all supporting documentation in a PDF format by e-mail to the HHSC HUB Program Office by or before the Courtesy Review of HUB Subcontracting Plan deadline in the Schedule of Events, cover page of this IFB.
Prices offered, as part of the Bidder's response, must be firm, fixed prices for the life of the Contract.

The pricing must be submitted only using Exhibit C - Pricing Sheet based on the description and the unit of measure(s) provided for each line item. The unit prices must include all IFB requirements, including, but not limited to, labor, equipment, materials, supplies and all related expenses.

Contractors are required to immediately implement any price decrease that become available during the Contract term. Contractor must notify the designated HHSC Contract Manager in writing so that a Purchase Order Change Notice or Contract Amendment may be processed.

Contractor must provide, in writing to the HHSC Contract Manager, a request for a price adjustment. The adjustment request must use the index and formula identified in Section 9.2.1 (Price Adjustment Index). Only contracts with renewals are eligible for CPI increases and must be completed prior to the start of the renewal period.

Contractor must provide supporting documentation to justify any price adjustment. Any request submitted that fails to use the formula above for calculating a price adjustment will not be considered a complete, properly submitted request and will be rejected.

If Contractor at any time during the term of the Contract provides a discount on the final contract costs, Contractor will notify HHSC in writing at least ten (10) calendar days prior to the effective date of the discount.
The request must be submitted to the HHSC Contract Manager in writing and include supporting documentation from the USDOL reflecting the increase and the effective date of the increase.

Contractor shall, within three (3) business days (or another date approved by HHSC of receipt of written notice of a non-material deficiency, provide the HHSC Contract Manager a written response that: a) Explains the reasons for the deficiency, Contractor's plan to address or cure the deficiency, and when the deficiency will be cured.

The Plan, at a minimum, must include, but is not limited to: a) A detailed explanation of the reasons for the cited deficiency; b) Contractor's assessment or diagnosis of the cause; and c) A specific proposal to cure or resolve the deficiency to include a timeline for implementation.
The Plan must be submitted by the deadline set forth in HHSC's request.

Contractor is required to correct all performance issues reported by the HHSC Contract Manager within 48 business hours. Contractor shall provide a written report detailing the performance issue(s) and resolution.

Mark the Original Proposal, on the top of the front page, with the words "CONTAINS CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION" in large, bold, capitalized letters (the size of, or equivalent to, 12-point Times New Roman font or arger); and

Identify, adjacent to each portion of the IFB Response, that Bidder claims is exempt from public disclosure, the claimed exemption from disclosure (NOTE: no redactions are to be made in the Original IFB Response).
Certify, in the designated section of the HHS Solicitation Affirmations, Bidder's confidential information assertion and the filing of its Public Information Act Copy; and
Submit a separate "Public Information Act Copy" of the Original Response (in addition to the original and all copies otherwise required under the provisions of this IFB).
The copy must be clearly marked as "PUBLIC INFORMATION ACT COPY" on the front page in large, bold, capitalized letters (the size of, or equivalent to, 12-point Times New Roman font or larger);
Each portion Bidder claims is exempt from public disclosure must be redacted (blacked out); and

Bidder must identify, adjacent to each redaction, the claimed exemption from disclosure. Each identification provided as required in Subsection (c) of this section must be identical to those set forth in the Original Response as required in Subsection (a)(2), above.
Bidder should not submit a Public Information Act Copy indicating that the entire proposal is exempt from disclosure.
IFB Responses should not be marked or asserted as copyrighted material.

Invoices submitted to HHSC must include the Contract or Purchase Order number and must describe the work completed, in detail, for which payment is requested. The detail of the work completed must comply with the Scope of Work and Pricing Sheet (see Exhibit C).
Contractor must submit invoices for services performed on a monthly basis or as otherwise indicated on the purchase order.
Separate invoices must be submitted for each service performed or deliverable, as applicable.
Notwithstanding any such dispute, Contractor must continue to perform the services and/or produce deliverables in compliance with the terms of the Contract.

Contractor may be required to submit bond documentation and current certificates of insurance or other proof acceptable to HHSC at the time of notification of a potential award and such proof must be received by the HHSC Contract Manager prior to execution by HHSC of any contract.

Contractor shall maintain the required insurance during the initial Contract term and any renewal or extension period exercised. Contractor shall be responsible for ensuring its subcontractors are in compliance with all applicable insurance and bond requirements.

Contractor shall carry insurance in the types and amounts indicated for the duration of the Contract. The insurance shall be evidenced by delivery to HHSC of certificates of insurance executed by the insurer or its authorized agent stating coverages, limits, expiration dates and compliance with all applicable required provisions.
Contractor shall update all expired policies prior to submission for monthly payment.
Contractor shall provide and maintain all insurance coverage with the minimum amounts described throughout the life of the Contract.
Contractor shall deliver to HHSC true and complete copies of certificates and corresponding policy endorsements within 10 days following award.

Coverage shall be written on an occurrence basis by companies authorized and admitted to do business in the State of Texas and rated A or better by A.M. Best Company or similar rating company or otherwise acceptable to HHSC.
This insurance shall not be canceled, materially changed, or non-renewed except after thirty (30) days' written notice has been given to HHSC.

The Health and Human Services Commission, its officials, directors, employees, representatives, and volunteers shall be added as additional insureds as respects operations and activities of, or on behalf of the named insured performed under Contract with HHSC. The additional insured status must cover completed operations as well.
A waiver of subrogation in favor of the Health and Human Services Commission shall be provided in all policies.

Without limiting any of the other obligations or liabilities of Contractor, Contractor shall require each Subcontractor performing work under the Contract to maintain, at Subcontractor's own expense, during the term of the Contract, the same stipulated minimum insurance including the required provisions and additional policy conditions as shown above.

Contractor must retain the certificates of insurance for the duration of the Contract plus seven (7) years and shall have the responsibility of enforcing these insurance requirements among its Subcontractors.

Workers' Compensation and Employer's Liability Insurance with limits as required by the Texas Workers' Compensation Act, with the policy endorsed to provide a waiver of subrogation in favor of the Health and Human Services Commission, employer's liability insurance of not less than: a) Employer's Liability: Each Accident $1,000,000 b) Disease: Each Employee $1,000,000 c) Disease: Policy Limit $1,000,000

Commercial General Liability... fully insuring Contractor's liability for bodily injury (including death) and property damage with a minimum limit of: a) $1,000,000 per occurrence; b) $2,000,000 general aggregate; c) $5,000 Medical Expense each person; d) $1,000,000 Personal Injury and Advertising Liability; e) $2,000,000 products and completed operations aggregate; f) $50,000 Damage to Premises Rented to You; and g) Coverage shall be on an "occurrence" basis.

Commercial Automobile Liability Covering owned, hired, and non-owned vehicles, with a minimum combined single limit for bodily injury (including death) and property damage of $1,000,000 per accident. No aggregate shall be permitted for this type of coverage.
Contractor shall obtain, pay for and maintain professional liability errors and omissions insurance during the Contract term, insuring Contractor for an amount of not less than $1,000,000.

Contractor shall obtain, pay for and maintain umbrella liability insurance during the Contract term, insuring Contractor for not less than $1,000,000 that provides coverage at least as broad as and applies in excess and follows form of the primary liability coverages required hereinabove.

An administrative screening of Responses timely received will be conducted by HHSC PCS to determine which Responses meet all IFB minimum requirements and are deemed responsive and qualified for further consideration and evaluation.

Note: Any disqualifying factor set forth in this IFB does not constitute an irregularity (e.g., Submission of Exhibit A HHS Solicitation Affirmations, and Exhibit F HSP, which must be completed, signed and submitted with the IFB Response) and will not be waived.

Responses shall be evaluated in accordance with Title 10, Subtitle D, Chapter 2155, Sections 2155.074, 2155.075(a), and 2155.144; and Chapter 2156, Section 2156.007, Texas Government Code; and Chapter 2157, Section 2157.003.

All Responses will be evaluated according to the following criteria: a) Bidder meeting or exceeding the requirements and specifications in accordance with this IFB; b) Bidder's ability to meet performance delivery requirements; and c) Price.

The pricing will be evaluated across all Bidders to determine the Response with the lowest price per line item or lowest total for all line items on Exhibit C – Pricing Sheet. The award will be made to the Bidder whose Response offers the best value to the State based on all factors considered, including price.
Bidders may be rejected as a result of unsatisfactory past performance under any contract(s) as reflected in vendor performance reports, reference checks, or other sources.

Evaluation will be based upon Bidder's demonstrated experience and ability to provide services and related goods. The evaluation may also consider the Bidder's demonstrated financial capability, financial solvency, and capacity to fulfil the requirements of this IFB.

Pursuant to Title 1 Texas Administrative Code (TAC), Part 15, Chapter 391, Subchapter D, Rule §391.405(a), contractors, respondents, and vendors interested in working with HHSC are required to implement standards of conduct to apply to all matters involving, or related to, those solicitations and contract(s) between themselves and HHSC.

Bidder represents and warrants that, if selected for award of a contract as a result of this IFB, Bidder shall submit to HHSC the signed Certificate of Interested Parties processed online through the Texas Ethics Commission (TEC) prior to contract award.

If the potential awardee does not timely submit a completed, certified, and signed TEC Form 1295 to HHSC, HHSC is prohibited by law from executing a contract, even if the potential awardee is otherwise eligible for award.
Responses submitted by facsimile, or any other method not specified in this IFB, will NOT be accepted or considered.
Responses sent by e-mail must be sent to: pcsbids@hhs.texas.gov.
The e-mail subject line must contain the IFB number, title as indicated on the cover page of this IFB and number of e-mails if more than one (e.g., 1 of #, etc.).

The body of each e-mail must include the following information: Bidder's name; Contact Name for Response; Phone number for Response Contact; IFB number from cover page of this IFB; Purchaser Name (Sole Point of Contact and Communications, Section 6.1).

All documents should be submitted in Microsoft Office® formats (Word® and Excel®, as applicable) or in a form that may be read by Microsoft Office® software. Any documents with signatures shall be submitted as an Adobe® portable document format (.pdf) file.
Files must be attachments to the email. Links and access given to file storage accounts are not permitted.
Attachments may not exceed 25 MB due to HHSC email file size requirements.
Submit one (1) USB drive of the complete Response package – hard copy Responses will not be accepted.
The USB drive must be enclosed in properly documented and sealed envelope or sealed carton.

The envelope or carton must be properly labeled, on the face or top of each, with the following: 1. Bidder's name 2. Contact Name for Response 3. Phone number for Response Contact 4. IFB number from the cover page of this IFB 5. HHSC PCS Purchaser Name (Sole Point of Contact and Communications, Section 6.1).

Failure to submit the following with the Response WILL disqualify the Bidder from further consideration for evaluation or award. Exhibit A - HHS Solicitation Affirmations (Pages 1-14), completed and signed
Failure to submit the following with the Response WILL disqualify the Bidder from further consideration for evaluation or award. Exhibit C - Pricing Sheet, completed
Failure to submit the following with the Response WILL disqualify the Bidder from further consideration for evaluation or award. Exhibit F - HUB Subcontracting Plan (HSP), completed and signed
Exhibit B-1 - Attachment 1 Security and Privacy Initial Inquiry (SPI) which must be completed and signed, if applicable.
Exhibit D – Bidder Reference and Contractor Qualifications Form, completed
Addendum Acknowledgement Form(s), if applicable
Public Information Act Copy of Response, if applicable. Reference Section 12.7 Public Information Act – Bidder Requirements Regarding Disclosure

Exhibit I– Form 4109 Application for Texas Identification Number, if applicable. Complete and return if no prior business has been done with HHSC or information has changed. Form 4109 is not required for bid submission to be compliant.
